title: Condensed exceptional inverse image of a reconstructed finite-level system
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$, and a $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. On a scheme $T$ equal to $X$ or $Y$, write $\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,T}=\varprojlim_n (\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_T$, and let $\mathcal I_T$ be the completed integral constructible category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$. Its rationalization has morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Let $J_T:\mathcal I_T[1/\ell]\simeq\mathcal C^c_E(T)$ be the scalar-extension realization of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Let $E_T^c=p_T^*C(-,\mathbf Q_\ell)$ and $\Omega_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous maps on the profinite set $S$ with values in one finite intermediate field of $\Omega/E$, as in [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category, prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Define the functor
$$U_T:\mathcal I_T\longrightarrow\mathcal C^c_\Omega(T),\qquad U_T(L)=\Omega_T^c\otimes^L_{E_T^c}J_T(L[1/\ell]).$$

Put $A_{n,T}=(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_T$ for $n\ge1$. Fix the chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. For $L\in\mathcal I_Y$ put $L_n=L\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,Y}}(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_Y$. Let $Rf_n^!$ denote the constructible exceptional inverse image obtained from the ordinary etale compact-support right adjoint by site comparison, as explicitly constructed for arbitrary $k$ in [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons]. Use the ordinary derived categories of strict varying-coefficient towers: a tower is a sequence of $A_{n,T}$-module sheaves with semilinear quotient transitions, and exactness is componentwise [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian, lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Let $\mathcal R_T$ be the actual derived reduction functor and $\mathcal L_T=R\varprojlim\,\operatorname{Res}$ its right adjoint [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; the limit is the total right derived inverse limit, not a choice of cones in a triangulated category [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. On ordinary etale towers let $F^{\mathrm{et}}=Rg_{*,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}j_{!,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}$ for the fixed compactification, and choose its Brown right adjoint $G^{\mathrm{et}}$ [lem-grothendieck-derived-brown-right-adjoint]. On bounded-below towers of etale origin write $G=\nu_{X,\bullet}^*G^{\mathrm{et}}R\nu_{Y,\bullet,*}$ whenever the displayed output is bounded below, using the ordinary tower site adjunction [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. For the data below this output is bounded below; put $N_\bullet=G(\mathcal R_YL)$. It has canonical identifications $N_n\simeq Rf_n^!L_n$, preserving counits, given by uniqueness of right adjoints [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint]; its transition adjoints are the ordinary finite coefficient mates of [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons, det-sp-unique-adjoint-coefficients]. No right adjoint on all ambient unbounded pro-etale complexes is asserted.

Suppose supplied a normalized tower $M_\bullet$ in the ordinary derived category of these pro-etale coefficient systems, with specified isomorphisms $\phi_n:M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!L_n$. Normalized means that the actual transition adjoints $M_m\otimes^L_{A_{m,X}}A_{n,X}\to M_n$ are invertible for $m\ge n$, with the quotient cocycle. Require that the $\phi_n$ intertwine these transitions with the exceptional-image quotient transitions. Require either (a) a specified isomorphism $\theta:M_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}N_\bullet$ in this ordinary derived category whose evaluations are $\phi_n$ under the preceding level identifications, or (b) one integer $r$ such that every $M_n$ has cohomology only in degree $r$. In (b), $\theta$ is constructed by good truncation to the degree-$r$ cohomology systems; an additional system isomorphism is not a hypothesis. In both cases use the actual ordinary tower counit $F M_\bullet\xrightarrow{F\theta}F N_\bullet\to\mathcal R_YL$, transported from the Brown adjunction, where $F$ is the proper/open functor on pro-etale towers. Suppose each cohomology sheaf of each level is constructible in the intrinsic finite-stratification sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], and the levels have a common finite cohomological interval independent of $n$. Assume $M=R\varprojlim M_\bullet$ lies in $\mathcal I_X$, with its canonical reductions identified with $M_n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Then there is a natural isomorphism
$$c_{f,L,M_\bullet}:U_X(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{!,\Omega}^{\,R}(U_YL).$$
Here $Rf_{!,\Omega}$ is the bounded constructible condensed-module compact-support functor, defined using extension by zero and proper direct image in the chosen Nagata compactification [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek], and $Rf_{!,\Omega}^{\,R}$ is its chosen right adjoint on $\mathcal C^c_\Omega$, namely the functor $Rf^!$ of [sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek] for the condensed ring $\underline\Omega$, that is $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleUpperShriek}(\mathrm{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell),\ell,f)$ at master commit 7347520d9b0d17cc31d0fc34ea20f1381a83fe13, with $X,Y$ viewed as the objects of $\operatorname{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)$ given by their structure maps and $f$ as the corresponding arrow over $k$ (the historical declaration has implicit $k$). More explicitly, fix the chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{g}Y$ and a right adjoint of its bounded constructible proper direct image $Rg_{*,\Omega}$, as required by the master declaration's left-adjoint instance. Then this right adjoint is $(Rg_{*,\Omega})^R$ followed by $j^*$, with the adjunction obtained by composing $j_!\dashv j^*$ and the chosen $Rg_{*,\Omega}\dashv(Rg_{*,\Omega})^R$. This assertion concerns this constructible right adjoint and asserts no unbounded ambient pro-etale adjoint. The isomorphism is the adjunction comparison: its counit is induced by the finite-level exceptional counits under completed reconstruction, localization and extension to $\Omega$. It is compatible with a refinement of the compactification and with morphisms of the supplied ordinary derived systems. Here such a morphism consists of a map of integral inputs and an actual derived-system map commuting with the identifications with the Brown exceptional towers. In case (b), for two data sets concentrated in the same degree r, commutation of the level-identification squares suffices for this system compatibility, because maps between degree-r cohomology diagrams are determined componentwise. In addition $U_T$ sends the integral coefficient object to the condensed tensor unit and commutes with shifts.

proof.text: Work uniformly over a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$; initially $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Finite type over the field gives local noetherianity, quasi-compactness and finite dimension by the cited geometric tools; a finite affine subcover gives noetherianity. Also $\ell$ is invertible. For every integral test object $K$, and for $L,M$, the stratified-perfect characterization gives, locally on finitely many strata, bounded finite-projective $R$-models $P$. The covering definition permits a finite affine refinement on each quasi-compact stratum. Take the extreme degrees of these finitely many models. Each reduction is represented locally by $P\otimes_R A_n$, a bounded complex of finite-projective, hence flat, coefficient sheaves. Its degrees lie in the same interval independently of $n$; its cohomology is locally a finite $A_n$-module. The bounded-flat K-flat theorem and derived change of rings justify these computations, including tensor with an arbitrary degree-zero module sheaf. Thus on each stratum all reductions have a common finite Tor interval and constructible cohomology.

proof.text: For completeness, assemble the Tor interval on the whole scheme. Inverse image commutes with the derived tensor under the constant-ring identifications. Covering-family detection therefore gives vanishing outside the chosen interval on each stratum. Write the finitely many locally closed strata as differences of closed subsets and cut successively along these closed subsets. Each final piece is contained in one stratum. At each cut the open-closed short exact sequence detects a zero cohomology sheaf from its two restrictions. Reversing the cuts proves the global vanishing. The open complements are quasi-compact by noetherianity. The same strata give intrinsic constructibility by the finite local models in Step 1. Membership in the integral category supplies etale-origin witnesses, so the reductions of all integral inputs and test objects lie in the finite bounded constructible finite-Tor categories. Zero objects and empty schemes may use the interval $[0,0]$.

proof.text: Let $\mathsf{Tow}^{\mathrm{et}}_T$ be modules over the ring system $(A_n)_n$ in the topos of inverse sequences on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, and similarly on the pro-etale site. These are categories of modules on small ringed sites, hence Grothendieck; kernels and cokernels are levelwise. Derived coproducts are represented by termwise sums, so evaluations preserve them and jointly detect isomorphisms. Form $F^{\mathrm{et}}=Rg_{*,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}j_{!,\bullet}^{\mathrm{et}}$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. The tower direct-image evaluation theorem gives $e_nF^{\mathrm{et}}=F_n^{\mathrm{et}}e_n$ on this whole category. Exact open extension and total right derived proper image are exact triangulated functors. At every level proper direct image preserves arbitrary coproducts; open extension does too because it is a left adjoint. Evaluating the canonical coproduct comparison for $F^{\mathrm{et}}$ therefore gives isomorphisms at every $n$, proving that comparison invertible. Brown representability for the Grothendieck source now gives $F^{\mathrm{et}}\dashv G^{\mathrm{et}}$. This is an ordinary derived adjunction, with its actual unit and counit. The scalar action on the right adjoint is the transpose of scalar multiplication through the $R$-linear left functor, making these Hom bijections $R$-linear.

proof.text:
Use the derived left adjoint $LE_n^T\dashv e_n$ with $(LE_n^TP)_q=P\otimes^L_{A_n}A_q$ for $q\le n$, zero otherwise. There is an actual natural map $\chi:LE_n^YF_n^{\mathrm{et}}\to F^{\mathrm{et}}LE_n^X$: its adjunct under $LE_n^Y\dashv e_n$ is the identity after $e_nF^{\mathrm{et}}LE_n^X=F_n^{\mathrm{et}}$. At $q\le n$ its evaluation is the canonical coefficient projection $F_n^{\mathrm{et}}P\otimes^L A_q\to F_q^{\mathrm{et}}(P\otimes^L A_q)$; at $q>n$ both objects vanish. This identification follows from the quotient transitions and the counit definition of the projection map. The proper projection formula for arbitrary finite-ring complexes and the extension-by-zero tensor formula make these evaluations invertible, so $\chi$ is an isomorphism. Consequently
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,e_nG^{\mathrm{et}}Q)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(LE_n^XP,G^{\mathrm{et}}Q)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F^{\mathrm{et}}LE_n^XP,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F_n^{\mathrm{et}}P,e_nQ).$$
Uniqueness of right adjoints identifies $e_nG^{\mathrm{et}}$ with the finite etale right adjoint and identifies the evaluated counit with its counit. Precompose this chain with the maps $\sigma_{mn}:LE_n(-\otimes^L A_n)\to LE_m$ from the evaluation lemma. Its explicit adjunct formula shows that the transition of $G^{\mathrm{et}}Q$ is the transpose of the coefficient-extended finite counit followed by the transition of $Q$. Thus these are precisely the finite exceptional coefficient mates. Ordinary mate pasting gives the quotient-composition identities; this compares actual maps and does not infer equality from evaluations.

proof.text: Under alternative (a) take the supplied ordinary derived-system isomorphism $\theta:M_\bullet\to N_\bullet$. Under (b), exact evaluations show that both systems have cohomology only in degree $r$. For a representative complex $C$, the functorial good truncations give quasi-isomorphisms $C\leftarrow\tau_{\le r}C\to H^r(C)[-r]$; the latter map is the quotient $\ker d^r\to\ker d^r/\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$. The transition squares for $\phi_n$ induce an isomorphism between the strict cohomology systems $H^r(M_\bullet)$ and $H^r(N_\bullet)$. Conjugating its shifted single-complex map by these truncations constructs $\theta$. Full faithfulness of the single-complex functor, also after shifting, shows that its evaluation is exactly $\phi_n$ and proves naturality for same-degree data sets. For alternative (a), naturality is the specified square with $\theta$. Transporting the Brown counit through $F\theta$ now gives the counit on $M_\bullet$ as a map in the ordinary tower derived category. General levelwise derived morphisms have not been lifted to system morphisms.

proof.text:
Write $P_R$ for compact-support reconstruction, with its actual ordinary-system comparison $\alpha_K:\mathcal R_Y(P_RK)\simeq F\mathcal R_XK$. For each integral $K$ use reduction/total-limit adjunction, $\theta$, the ordinary Brown adjunction transported as in Step 5, and $\alpha_K$ to obtain
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,M)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathsf{Tow}_X)}(\mathcal R_XK,M_\bullet)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathsf{Tow}_Y)}(F\mathcal R_XK,\mathcal R_YL)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_Y(P_RK,\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YL)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_Y(P_RK,L).$$
The last identification uses the inverse of the actual reduction-adjunction unit $u_L$. Its composite to level $n$ is the quotient map, hence it is the derived-completeness comparison and is invertible. The chain is $R$-linear, natural in all integral test objects and in the supplied data. Its counit $t:P_RM\to L$ is the image of $1_M$. Explicitly its tower reduction is the composite $F\mathcal R_XM\xrightarrow{F e_M}FM_\bullet\xrightarrow{F\theta}FN_\bullet\xrightarrow{\epsilon}\mathcal R_YL$, conjugated by $\alpha_M$, where $e_M:\mathcal R_X\mathcal L_XM_\bullet\to M_\bullet$ is the reduction-adjunction counit. The assumed canonical reduction identifications make $e_M$ invertible. The projection identities for this adjunction show that $t_n$ is exactly $\epsilon_n\circ F_n(\phi_n)$. All equalities are of ordinary system maps before taking the total right derived limit; no inverse system of enhanced mapping complexes is invoked.

proof.text:
The rationalized categories have the same objects and integral Hom groups tensored with $E$. Tensor the two inverse $R$-linear bijections of Step 7 with $E$; their composites remain identities. The functor and transformation extensions send $h/t^a$ to $F(h)/t^a$, so this also preserves naturality and the counit. Transport through the $E$-linear realization equivalences $J_X,J_Y$ and the compact-support comparison $a$. Every condensed $E$-test object $C$ has an integral lattice, so the result is, for every such $C$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_E(C,J_X(M[1/t]))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_E(P_E^cC,J_Y(L[1/t])).$$
Its counit is the image of $t$. This is representability at the supplied $L$, not an assumption that a right adjoint preserves all integral constructible objects.

proof.text:
Let $E\subset H$ be finite, put $S=\mathcal O_H$, choose a uniformizer $v$, and write $tS=v^eS$. Ordinary derived tensor $L_S=L\otimes^L_{\widehat R}\widehat S$, $M_S=M\otimes^L_{\widehat R}\widehat S$ agrees with completed integral extension by the finite-free comparison. The integral extension theorem and the stratified-perfect characterization put them in $\mathcal I(S)$. Tensor computations and associators use K-flat resolutions; on a ringed system site these are the ordinary change-of-rings functors. Apply scalar extension to the actual integral counit of Step 7 and use the compact-support comparison to form
$$t_S:P_SM_S\simeq(P_RM)_S\xrightarrow{t\otimes1}L_S.$$
On cofinal quotients $S/t^nS=S/v^{en}$ its reduction is the scalar extension of the finite counit. The finite exceptional mate equation identifies its transpose with the finite-free scalar extension of $\phi_n$, followed by that mate. These are isomorphisms. This statement uses only the ordinary functors and counit identities asserted by the finite comparison lemma. It neither extends an enhanced section nor assumes that tensoring with the nonflat quotient $S/v^m$ preserves degree-$r$ concentration.

proof.text:
For every $m$ choose $n$ with $en\ge m$ and reduce $t_S$ further from $S/v^{en}$ to $S/v^m$. The finite quotient mate equation identifies its transpose with the further coefficient extension of the preceding isomorphism followed by the quotient mate, hence it is invertible. For two choices of $n$, pass to a common larger index; the quotient-composition identities identify the transposes. Now construct a single map, rather than lifting those finite transposes: use $\alpha_{M_S}$ to view $\mathcal R_Y(t_S)$ as a map $F_S\mathcal R_XM_S\to\mathcal R_YL_S$, and take its ordinary Brown-adjunction transpose
$$\theta_S:\mathcal R_XM_S\longrightarrow G_S(\mathcal R_YL_S).$$
Step 4 identifies each evaluation with exactly the finite transpose just computed. It is therefore an isomorphism by conservativity of evaluation. The output of the Brown adjoint has the common bounds of the reductions of $M_S$, so the site transport of Step 5 applies. Thus alternative (a) is available over $H$, even if alternative (b) was used initially. Steps 7–8 over $H$ give the representing Hom bijections for every condensed $H$-test object. Under a further finite extension, both reconstructed counits are the extension of $t$ by tensor associativity and the compact-support coefficient comparison. Uniqueness of transposition and ordinary mate pasting identify the corresponding bijections. This proves their coefficient compatibility as actual transformations.

proof.text: Return to $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Every object $C$ of $\mathcal C^c_\Omega(X)$ descends to a finite field $H/E$. The two-colimit theorem identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(C,U_XM)$ with the filtered colimit of $\operatorname{Hom}_{H'}(C_{H'},M_{H'}^{\mathrm{rat}})$ over finite $H'\supset H$. Apply the compatible bijections of Step 10. Compact-support scalar comparison identifies their other side with the filtered colimit of $\operatorname{Hom}_{H'}((P_H^cC_H)_{H'},L_{H'}^{\mathrm{rat}})$, namely $\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(P_\Omega^cC,U_YL)$. The inverse maps are compatible too, so the colimits are inverse bijections. Descent of morphisms and eventual equality prove independence of representatives and naturality. The counit $t_\Omega:P_\Omega^cU_XM\to U_YL$ is the image of $t$. This uses precisely the finite-extension-valued condensed ring of the master declaration.

proof.text: The authenticated historical master uses objects of $\operatorname{Over}(\operatorname{Spec}k)$; the given structure maps and $k$-linearity of $f$ supply exactly those objects and arrow. Let $J$ be the chosen condensed constructible right adjoint in the statement, with counit $\epsilon^J$. Define $c:U_XM\to J(U_YL)$ to be the $J$-transpose of $t_\Omega$. For every $C$, postcomposition with $c$ is the representation of Step 11 followed by the chosen adjunction and is bijective. Choose $a:J(U_YL)\to U_XM$ mapping to its identity; then $ca=1$. Injectivity on $\operatorname{Hom}(U_XM,U_XM)$ gives $ac=1$. Thus $c$ is the required isomorphism and $\epsilon^J\circ P_\Omega^c(c)=t_\Omega$. For maps of supplied systems, the ordinary tower Hom chain of Step 7, and then scalar extension, identify both transposes of the naturality square. Hence the square commutes by injectivity of transposition. In alternative (b) its system square is provided by Step 6. This proves naturality of the specified comparison, with the specified chosen adjunction.

proof.text: For a refinement $v:c^1\to c^2$, form the proper/open square with top and bottom the open immersions of $X$ and vertical maps $1_X$ and $v$. The ordinary tower comparison constructs the actual derived map $\Gamma_v:J_{i_2}R_{1_X}^{\mathcal T}\to R_v^{\mathcal T}J_{i_1}$ by fibre-product restriction, projection to the open-and-closed image, and open adjunction; it is invertible on bounded-below etale-origin towers and evaluates to the normalized finite proper/open comparison [lem-sp-proper-open-tower-comparison]. Applying $R_{c^2,*}^{\mathcal T}$ to $\Gamma_v$ with the direct-image compositor gives the refinement map. The formal coherence node, instantiated with these $P=R(-)_*^{\mathcal T}$, $J=(-)_!$ and $\Gamma_v$, proves identity, composition, common-refinement independence and cocycle, and compatibility with composition staircases [lem-sp-compactification-refinement-coherence]. Hence the ordinary etale compact-support comparison transports through an actual tower map, and the compact-support realization preserves it. Finite exceptional mates, ordinary mate pasting, and counit-preserving uniqueness transport the representing pair and coefficient maps [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons, lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison, det-sp-unique-right-adjoint, det-sp-unique-adjoint-coefficients, lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting, lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Reconstruction, rationalization and scalar extension preserve these named maps. For the condensed $q:P^1\xrightarrow{\sim}P^2$, the reconstructed counits satisfy $t^1_\Omega=t^2_\Omega q_{U_XM}$. Its mate $\rho:J^2\to J^1$ from $\epsilon^2q_{J^2}$ has inverse given by transposing $q^{-1}$; equal transposes show $c^1=\rho c^2$. No equality of tower maps is inferred from finite evaluations.
